entities.name: Suboccipital release reduces sympathetic activity
observations: Suboccipital release is described as an autonomic inhibition technique that reduces sympathetic influence and supports parasympathetic activity.
In an acutely ill patient, it is the lowest-load autonomic option among the listed techniques if respiratory and hemodynamic status are stable.

entities.name: Acute pneumonia requires medical stabilization
observations: Bilateral interstitial infiltrates with fever and dyspnea require urgent evaluation, oxygenation assessment, diagnostic work-up, and disease-specific treatment; OMT is adjunctive.
Evidence that suboccipital release improves acute pneumonia outcomes is limited and indirect.

entities.name: Suboccipital release
observations: Gentle occipito-atlantal decompression/inhibition is the best answer when the question asks for a technique to decrease sympathetic activity.
